statement: UNESCO's Matobo Hills inscription describes Mwari worship as a living oracular shrine tradition in that Zimbabwean landscape, associated with sacred sites and current community observance; the document only speculates that the religion may reach the Iron Age.

sources.citation: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, 'Matobo Hills' (World Heritage 306rev), sections Brief synthesis and Criterion vi, https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/306/
sources.author: UNESCO World Heritage Centre / Zimbabwe heritage authorities
sources.access_note: UNESCO text directly read: calls Mwari a practiced oracular tradition, connects it to shrines, and says it *may* date to the Iron Age. Page separates older rock art and archaeology from contemporary shrines.

does_not_demonstrate: UNESCO's conditional 'may date to the Iron Age' is not an established origin date.
Much older rock art and occupation at Matobo cannot be assigned to current Mwari practice.
This site-level source does not show continuous Mwari cult worship at Great Zimbabwe specifically.
adversarial_counter: Connecting later Matobo Mwari observance to specific Iron Age or medieval sites needs independent archaeological and textual corroboration.
notes: Institutional-source audit. Scope: named public page and its content only; no tradition founding-year inference. Independent historical / community review required before status change.
